_comment: What this corpus holds and declines to advise on, as data. The records stay in the corpus, query.py still lists them, each labelled as out of scope, and validate.py checks them like any other; what is kept out is the consultation. Kept beside the other tables for the reason locus-map.json is: validate.py --corpus DIR checks a corpus against its own scope, and a constant in a script would check a different corpus against this bundle's decision.
_why_handset_exposures: The standing decision keeps handsets out of scope: the handset is the one plane this corpus declines to advise on, while the mobile management plane (app.mdm, MANAGEMENT) stays in. The catalogue generators write handset records all the same, because the catalogue lists them, and until consult.py listed exposures only query.py showed them. consult.py refuses them from its EXPOSURE blocks and counts them as handset= on EXPOSURES_NOT_LISTED, so the refusal is visible rather than silent. Keyed by who.vendor exactly as the records file it. An exposure is a handset record when its vendor is listed here and every platform its products name matches one of the vendor's terms as whole words: products are split on commas and on 'and', so 'iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS' is refused while 'iOS and macOS' is a macOS exposure as well and stays listable. '*' refuses every exposure filed under the vendor, which for Android is the handset operating system and its parts. Code Aurora's ACDB audio driver is the Qualcomm Android audio driver. validate.py refuses a vendor here with no exposure filed under it, and a term matching none of that vendor's products, so the table cannot rot into refusing nothing; a handset record from a vendor not listed here is not caught, and is added here when it arrives.
_why_handset_names: The question side of the same decision. handset_exposures refuses records, so a bare handset name that resolves nothing was refused only when it happened to reach one by its product name, and "iPhone", which no record carries, was told to add the alias the decision forbids. A word here is refused when it is among the words of a question that resolved no vendor, product or class: consult.py answers UNRESOLVED, says the word is listed here, and points at the mobile management plane, which is in scope. Beside a vendor, product or class it refuses nothing, so "Cisco ASA VPN users on iOS phones", "iOS MDM" and the Guardsquare question are answered for what they name; beside a sector it refuses all but a word handset_names_also_places lists, so "iOS in government" is refused and "banks in Mali" is answered. Beside a word written as a name that reached no record and is no refused alias's it still refuses, and says that word decides the plane: "Kandji for iOS" names a management product, which is in scope, and "Pegasus iOS" spyware on the handset, which is not, and nothing in the word tells them apart, so consult.py offers it as the product to add with class app.mdm only on the condition that it manages the devices. When any such word stopped the refusal, any word that reached nothing did, and "iOS spyware" was told to add spyware as an alias; an ordinary word, written with no capital or digit, is no name. Wherever a word here stands in a question it does not refuse, consult.py and query.py say never to add it. A word here names what the table files as a handset, not every use of it: the one Snapdragon record lists laptop, vehicle and module parts beside the handset ones. consult.py also reads it beside a resolved vendor, where an EXPOSURES_ONLY answer would otherwise send a handset question to the endpoint plane its exposures' classes name. Mali and Snapdragon are the table's own terms for Arm and Qualcomm. A word is listed rather than derived from the product names the table refuses, because that was measured and refused: "gpu", "audio" and "chipsets" stand in those names and were answered as handset questions. One lower-case word each, because it is matched against the question's unresolved words; validate.py refuses a word an unambiguous alias would consume, which could never be refused, so "android", a vendor alias, is the vendor path's and not this list's. Not an alias: it resolves nothing.
_why_handset_names_also_places: The words of handset_names that also name a place: mali is Arm's GPU and a country. Beside a resolved sector such a word is read as the place and refuses nothing, so "banks in Mali" and "Mali government ministries" are answered for the sector they name; bare, or beside nothing that resolved, it is the table's handset name still. Every other handset name refuses beside a sector: when any sector stopped the refusal, "iOS in government" and "iOS banking apps" counted Apple's handset records prose-only, handset=0, and were told to add an alias. validate.py refuses a word here that handset_names does not list.
